item.title: Low-Temperature Sampling via Equilibrium Disagreements
item.description: arXiv:2611.08416v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a new framework for sampling at low temperatures using Glauber dynamics. In this regime, the coexistence of competing modes (commonly referred to as phases) creates bottlenecks that can make worst-case mixing exponentially slow. The main new ingredient in our framework is to relate convergence within a phase to the geometry of disagreements between two independent configurations drawn from that phase. As applications of our approach, we consider three canonical models on random regular graphs that have been central to low-temperature sampling, and establish fast convergence from natural initialisations of Glauber dynamics for every fixed degree. We show: --- For the hard-core model on random bipartite $d$-regular graphs, Glauber dynamics initialised from either one-sided independent set mixes within the corresponding phase in $n^{3/2+o(1)}$ steps throughout the non-uniqueness regime $\lambda>\lambda_c(d)$. --- For the random-cluster model on random $d$-regular graphs, for every real $q>2$, Glauber dynamics initialised from the all-in edge set mixes within the ordered phase in $n^{3/2+o(1)}$ steps for all $\beta\geq \beta_c$. Similarly, Glauber dynamics initialised from the all-out edge set mixes within the disordered phase in $n^{3/2+o(1)}$ steps for $\beta\leq \beta_c$. --- For the ferromagnetic Ising model on random $d$-regular graphs, Glauber dynamics initialised from all-plus or all-minus mixes within the corresponding phase in $n^{3/2+o(1)}$ steps throughout the low-temperature regime $\beta>\beta_c(d)$. We also give an $n^{2+o(1)}$-time algorithm that combines phase samples into samples from the full distribution, avoiding in particular time-costly approximations of the corresponding partition functions to the target sampling accuracy.
item.dc:creator: Andreas Galanis, Daniel Stefankovic

item.title: Diameter bounds for complexes that are close to flag or close to normal
item.description: arXiv:2611.08071v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The Hirsch problem asks how large the diameter of the dual graph of a simplicial complex can be, in terms of its number of vertices. For normal complexes, the classical bounds are the Larman-Barnette bound, which is linear for fixed dimension, the Kalai-Kleitman bound, which is quasi-polynomial, and the Adiprasito-Benedetti bound n-d, which however holds only for flag complexes. After sharpening the Larman-Barnette and the Kalai-Kleitman bounds, we study how the three bounds deteriorate when flagness or normality is weakened. We give three ways to quantify the distance from flagness, and in each case we bound the diameter in a way that interpolates between the Adiprasito-Benedetti and the Larman-Barnette bounds. We also quantify the distance from normality by a parameter q, and obtain a bound that is a polynomial of degree q in n. Finally, we conjecture a statement on flag layered families that would imply an interpolation between the Adiprasito-Benedetti and the Kalai-Kleitman bounds.
item.dc:creator: Bruno Benedetti, Giuliamaria Menara

item.title: First-Order Model Checking on Monadically Dependent Graph Classes
item.description: arXiv:2611.08143v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Monadically dependent graph classes are those in which first-order logic cannot encode all graphs. They include all nowhere dense classes and all classes of bounded twin-width. We show that first-order model checking is fixed-parameter tractable on every monadically dependent graph class. Together with the known hardness result for hereditary classes that are not monadically dependent, this gives a complete characterization of the hereditary graph classes with fixed-parameter tractable first-order model checking. This resolves a central open problem in algorithmic model theory. Our proof combines ideas from structural graph theory (graph decompositions), finite model theory (locality of first-order logic), and model theory (counting types). In particular, we show that in monadically dependent classes, tuples of fixed length have only $|U|^{O(1)}$ types of fixed quantifier rank over any set of parameters $U$.
item.dc:creator: Jan Dreier, Nikolas M\"ahlmann, Szymon Toru\'nczyk

item.title: Hardness of integer linear feasibility with cyclic support
item.description: arXiv:2611.08304v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that integer linear feasibility is strongly $NP$-complete even when the constraint matrix has exactly two nonzero entries in every row and column, with its support forming a single cycle. This holds already for monotone systems (one positive and one negative coefficient in each inequality) with nonzero coefficients of absolute value $2$ or $3$ and right-hand sides in $\{-1,0,1,2\}$. No variable bounds are supplied separately from the system. For systems in which each inequality involves at most two variables, this strengthens known hardness results by restricting all numerical data to fixed finite sets. For systems in which each variable occurs in at most two inequalities, this establishes, to the best of our knowledge, the first $NP$-hardness result for feasibility. We also give negative answers, unless $P=NP$, to questions on polynomial-time solvability of integer programs with bounded coefficients and bounded totally $\Delta$-modular treewidth, and on fixed-parameter tractability of integer bound propagation with respect to coefficient and right-hand-side magnitudes.
item.dc:creator: Marco Di Summa

item.title: Mutual-visibility k-colouring is NP-complete for every fixed diameter
item.description: arXiv:2611.01012v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A mutual-visibility set in a graph G is a set S of vertices such that any two vertices of S are connected by a shortest path with no internal vertex in S, and the mutual-visibility chromatic number $\chi_\mu(G)$ is the minimum number of mutual-visibility sets needed to partition V(G). Babu, Di Stefano and Lakshmanan showed that it is NP-complete to decide whether $\chi_\mu(G)\le 2$ for graphs of diameter four. We show that the problem remains NP-complete for graphs of diameter d, for every fixed $d\ge2$; diameter two is the smallest diameter for which the problem is non-trivial. More generally, for all fixed $k\ge2$ and $d\ge2$, it is NP-complete to decide whether $\chi_\mu(G)\le k$ for graphs of diameter d. The proof rests on a reformulation of $\chi_\mu(G)\le 2$ for diameter-two graphs as the 2-colourability of an associated hypergraph, and on a reduction from 2-colourability of 3-uniform hypergraphs without short cycles.
item.dc:creator: Siddhesh Chaubal

item.title: On rigid regular graphs and a problem of Babai and Pultr
item.description: arXiv:2502.11421v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A graph is rigid if it only admits the identity endomorphism. We show that for every $d\ge 3$ there exist infinitely many mutually rigid $d$-regular graphs of arbitrary odd girth $g\geq 7$. Moreover, we determine the minimum order of a rigid $d$-regular graph for every $d\ge 3$. This provides strong positive answers to a question of van der Zypen [https://mathoverflow.net/q/296483, https://mathoverflow.net/q/321108]. Further, we use our construction to show that every finite monoid is isomorphic to the endomorphism monoid of a regular graph. This solves a problem of Babai and Pultr [J. Comb. Theory, Ser. B, 1980].
item.dc:creator: Kolja Knauer, Gil Puig i Surroca

item.title: The only Class 0 Flower snark is the smallest
item.description: arXiv:2505.22941v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In graph pebbling, pebbles are distributed across the vertices of a graph. A pebbling move consists of removing two pebbles from one vertex and adding one pebble to an adjacent vertex. The pebbling number is the minimum number $t$ such that, regardless of how the $t$ pebbles are initially placed, it is always possible to perform a sequence of moves that results in at least one pebble placed on any specified target vertex. Graphs whose pebbling number is equal to the number of vertices are called Class~$0$ and provide a challenging set of graphs that resist being characterized. In this note, we answer a question recently proposed by the pioneering study on the pebbling number of snark graphs: we prove that the smallest Flower snark $J_3$ is Class~$0$, establishing that $J_3$ in fact is the only Class~$0$ Flower snark. that systematically reduce the space of pebble configurations. Our bound-based approach shows particular promise for diameter $3$ graphs, where the neighborhood structure remains sufficiently constrained to enable effective analysis.
item.dc:creator: Guilherme Adamatti Bridi, Andr\'e Luis Alves Martins, Franklin de Lima Marquezino, Celina Miraglia Herrera de Figueiredo

item.title: A Resolution of Friedgut's Conjecture on Influential Coalitions
item.description: arXiv:2609.16401v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove that, for every constant $\varepsilon>0$ and every function $f:\Sigma^n\to\{0, 1\}$, there is a coalition of $O(n/\sqrt{\log n})$ coordinates and a target output $b\in\{0, 1\}$ such that, after the remaining coordinates are sampled uniformly and independently, the coalition can choose its values to make the output equal to $b$ with probability at least $1-\varepsilon$. The bound is independent of the alphabet size and also holds for monotone Boolean functions on $[0,1]^n$, resolving a conjecture of Friedgut (Combinatorics, Probability and Computing, 2004). Unlike the Boolean cube setting, where Kahn, Kalai, and Linial (FOCS, 1988) give a coalition bound of $O(n/\log n)$, no sublinear bound independent of the alphabet size was previously known. In collective coin flipping, our result gives the first sublinear bound on the number of bad players needed to force a fixed output with probability at least $1-\varepsilon$ in any one-round protocol with independent uniform messages, regardless of the message length. A key ingredient in our proof is an encoding that lets us relate the influence of a function on a product space to the $p$-biased influence of the encoded function. We then rely on a structure theorem of Hatami (Annals of Mathematics, 2012) for functions with small $p$-biased influence to bias the encoded function.
item.dc:creator: Eshan Chattopadhyay, Mohit Gurumukhani

item.title: Product Expansion of Random Codes via Analytic Techniques
item.description: arXiv:2610.02512v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Beginning with the work of Dinur, Lin, and Vidick (FOCS, 2024), tensor codes with constant product expansion have been foundational to recent advances in quantum locally testable codes (qLTCs) based on cubical complexes. Informally, product expansion says that any low-weight parity check of the tensor code can be written as the sum of few parity checks of each component code in each dimension. Recent work of Kalachev and Panteleev (FOCS, 2025) showed that tensors of random linear codes have constant product expansion. In this work we initiate the study of random linear codes with prescribed automorphism groups. For every sufficiently large prime $k$, we construct pairs of rate $1/2$ MDS codes of length $2k$, over finite fields whose size depends on $k$, that have constant two-sided product expansion and are invariant under the simultaneous cyclic shift of two cycles of length $k$. This shift is the local action in the cube complexes of Rungtanapirom, Stix, and Vdovina (Internat. J. Algebra Comput., 2019). Along the way we give a proof of the existence of two-sided product expanding codes which, unlike the earlier result of [KP25], does not rely on explicit constructions of asymptotically optimal locally testable codes. Our proof relies on several new techniques that we view as interesting in their own right. Instead of working directly over finite fields, we work over the reals and use random Rademacher matrices for the generator matrices of the component codes. From here, we show how to relate product expansion to the operator norm of sparse restrictions of carefully chosen Gram matrices, which we bound using tools from random matrix theory. More generally, we propose a method for studying properties of random linear codes by lifting to random codes over $\mathbb{R}$ and $\mathbb{C}$, which we anticipate will be applicable more broadly to existential problems in coding theory.
item.dc:creator: Eshan Chattopadhyay, Noam Ringach, Nicholas Spooner

item.title: Exact Agreement Expansion up to the Top via Non-polarity
item.description: arXiv:2611.03261v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Agreement expansion asks whether local assignments to faces of a poset that usually agree on a sampled common face must agree with a single global function on most faces. Agreement expansion is exact (approximate) if local assignments need to exactly (approximately) agree with the global function. We suggest a new proof technique for agreement expansion that enables agreement expansion in settings which were previously beyond reach, such as: exact agreement expansion for Grassmannian posets (before only simplicial complexes support exact agreement expansion); agreement expansion based on assignments to top faces of the a complex (before agreement expansion is generally proven only for assignments to low dimensional faces); agreement expansion from one-sided spectral expansion (before, two sided spectral assumption was needed in general settings). Specifically, for down-closed simplicial and Grassmannian complexes, we prove an exact agreement theorem between any two layers assuming one-sided spectral expansion in links of singletons. As an application, we show that full bases of every rank-$k$ matroid admit exact agreement with soundness $O(k^2/[h(k-h)])$ when tested through $h$-element independent sets. We also obtain exact agreement on Grassmannian posets under one-sided spectral expansion, with stronger soundness under a local distance guarantee. Our key proof ideas center around non-polarity of the distributions of local assignments, probed via a random exposure of elements.
item.dc:creator: Tali Kaufman, Huy Tuan Pham
